title: Three Guests and a Bold Bargain
overview: Abraham welcomes three mysterious visitors who promise Sarah a son, and then he pleads with the LORD to spare the city of Sodom.

parts.label: Welcoming the strangers (vv. 1-8)
parts.note: In that culture a host simply stood up for ordinary visitors and walked out to meet only those of higher rank, yet Abraham runs to them, bows to the ground, offers water for dusty feet, and has a calf prepared, a rare honor since meat was saved for important guests. He also stands nearby while they eat, a mark of respect, all before he knows who they really are.

parts.label: Who the visitors are (vv. 1-2, 13)
parts.note: The story calls them three men, yet the LORD speaks through one of them, and interpreters are unsure whether all three are angels or one is God himself. Some Christians have read the chief visitor as an appearance of Christ before his birth, while a New Testament letter simply points to this scene as a reason to welcome strangers.

parts.label: Sarah laughs (vv. 9-15)
parts.note: The strangers know Sarah's name and promise she will have a son within a year, though she is long past childbearing age, so she laughs to herself in disbelief and then denies it out of fear. The LORD answers by asking whether anything is too hard for him, and the son's later name, Isaac, means "he laughs."

parts.label: God shares his plan (vv. 16-21)
parts.note: The LORD chooses to tell Abraham about Sodom because Abraham is meant to teach his family to do what is right and just. The cry rising from Sodom and Gomorrah is usually understood as the cry of people being wronged there, and the LORD speaking of going down to see for himself is human language showing that the judgment is not hasty.

parts.label: Abraham pleads for Sodom (vv. 22-33)
parts.note: Abraham boldly asks whether the Judge of all the earth will kill the innocent along with the guilty, and he bargains the number down from fifty innocent people to ten. Why he stops at ten is not explained, and the next chapter shows that not even ten were found.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether Abraham's pleading actually changed God's course or instead drew out a mercy God already intended to show.
think: When something seems unfair, is it right to push back, even against someone with far more power than you?
